title: Interpretation Act 1978
version: as in force at 21 April 2023 (reprint REPI005, the version the register's landing page offered as current on the retrieval date)
version_kind: reprint REPI005, status In Force on the landing page; the as-at date is read from the document cover
version_basis: the document's cover ('As in force at 21 April 2023'), the PDF's cover (the same words), and the landing page's Word and PDF links (id=11865), landing page status 'In Force', reprint 'REPI005'
why: Rules for reading and applying Northern Territory Acts and subordinate legislation: definitions, commencement, amendment and repeal, construction, the computation of time, statutory functions, and the citation of laws.
converter: macOS textutil (textutil -convert txt) followed by a short Python 3 script (not kept) that removes Word field codes, running heads and footers, page breaks, blank lines and leading and trailing spaces
conversion: the register's Word download, stored as 11865.doc, converted with textutil -convert txt; the script then removed 112 page-reference field codes (the page numbers they gave were kept), 1 table-of-contents field code, the trailing block of running heads and footers (11 lines of header and footer field text, 54 blank lines), 3 page breaks, 4 further blank lines, and leading spaces on 14 lines and trailing spaces or tabs on 4 lines; the output was checked word for word against pdftotext -layout of the PDF rendering
note: The register's Word download is a binary Word 97-2003 .doc served at an extensionless URL as application/msword; it was stored as 11865.doc before conversion.
pdf_use: cross-check of the converted text only; the PDF is not deposited
notes: The landing page states no 'as in force' date. It shows Status: In Force and Reprint: REPI005, links the Word and PDF files for id=11865, and leaves the Act No, Assent, Gazette No and Gazette Date fields blank. The as-at date 21 April 2023 is read from the cover of the Word document and of the PDF, which agree; the PDF's creation date and the Word file's last-modified date are also 21 April 2023.

The as-at date is 21 April 2023 and the retrieval date is 11 November 2026; the landing page's HTML names one reprint only (REPI005). Its amendment panel is loaded by script (/api/sitecore/Legislation/Amendment) and was not fetched, so any amendment list the page shows was not read.

The reprint's table of provisions and its ENDNOTES (1 Key, 2 List of legislation, 3 Savings and transitional provisions, 4 General amendments, 5 List of amendments) are kept, as in the Administration and Probate Act 1969 deposit. The last entry of the table of provisions is the ENDNOTES entry on line 142, and the endnotes themselves begin at line 963. Section 55(6) of the Act says an endnote is not part of the Act. Cutting the text from line 963 to the end leaves the Act and its Schedule.

Tables: textutil flattens Word tables, so no table is rendered as '| a | b |' rows. The PDF's structure tree holds one Table element, the List of legislation in the endnotes, and no Figure or Formula element, and the PDF holds no images (pdfimages -list), so the Act's body and Schedule contain no table, formula or image. In the endnotes the Key appears one row per line with cells separated by tabs, the List of legislation one cell per line, and the List of amendments as two tab-separated columns.

Characters kept as they are in the Word document: non-breaking spaces (U+00A0), en dashes (U+2013), non-breaking hyphens (U+2011) in 'Governor-General's' (s 6), 're-enacts' (s 15), 'Self-Government' (s 17) and 'by-law' (s 63A), and one right single quotation mark (U+2019, s 23A). A search for those words with an ordinary hyphen will not match the four U+2011 places.

The title lines 'NORTHERN TERRITORY OF AUSTRALIA', the Act's title and 'As in force at 21 April 2023' appear twice, once on the cover before the table of provisions and once before the long title, as in the Word document.

Comparison with the PDF rendering (pdftotext -layout): the Act and its Schedule agree word for word, and so does the table of provisions, page numbers included; the only differences are line-end hyphenation of three compound words in the PDF layout ('last-mentioned' twice, 'Self-Government' once). The endnotes were compared as a bag of words: they agree except that the PDF prints 's3' where the Word text has 's 3' in the list of amendments.
